benign.quirk: collects small bones and arranges them by size
benign.note: {They} got quiet once, lining up bird bones on a flat stone, smallest to largest. {They} said it helps {them} think. Nobody asked what about.

benign.quirk: keeps a smooth stone and talks to it like an old friend

benign.quirk: whispers when no one is listening

benign.quirk: whispers names of people who aren't here, like a roll call

benign.quirk: always leaves one empty seat at the fire, and gets tense if someone takes it
benign.note: {They} set out a spare log at the fire every evening and go quiet if anyone sits on it. No explanation offered. The log stays empty. The fire doesn't care.

benign.quirk: avoids still water — won't meet the reflection

malicious.quirk: smiles a beat too long when someone gets hurt
malicious.note: When the pot tipped and scalded Mara's hand, everyone flinched — except {first}, who smiled. Just a beat too long. {They} covered it by fetching water, quick and helpful.

malicious.quirk: remembers exactly what everyone owes, to the calorie

{first} did storm cleanup for six years, chainsaw first. {They} learned to work fast around widow-makers and to never rush the last cut.

{first} kept the night bus on schedule for eighteen years. {They} know the city by its streetlights and its last-call crowds.

{first} walked the train in every kind of weather for twenty years. {They} learned to read the sky, the schedule, and the crew's mood in one look.

questTemplates: You're awake. Don't sit up fast — you were out a full day. Woke up wanting {hope}.
I woke up in a clearing with eleven strangers and one {an_occ} — me. First thing I did was count heads — old {occ} habit, I guess. All I wanted was {hope}.
We have to decide — {first} says together, or starving separately. I'm {an_occ}, not a leader, but someone has to say it.
I'm {first}. I keep the fire lit and the arguments short — learned that as {an_occ}. Both are full-time jobs.
Nobody here chose this. But everybody here chose to stay past the first night — {first} counted. That counts for something. Me, I'm still hoping {hope}.
We found you on the {origin} side of the clearing — {first} was on watch. Someone carried you in. I know who; {first} isn't telling.

warm: Hey. Hey, you're awake. Don't sit up fast — you were out cold when we found you.
I'm {first}. I was {an_occ}, back in {origin}. Whatever's going on, none of us understand it either.
There's food by the fire and water in the clay pots. Eat first, questions later. You're safe here — well. Safer than out there.
Rest as long as you need. Nobody here is keeping score — we just got you back, and that's enough for today.
You look like hell, friend. That's a compliment — means you're alive enough to look like anything.
I'm {first}. Before all this I was {an_occ} in {origin}. Now? Now I'm the one who tells new folks the stew's not poisoned. It's not. Eat.
debt: Up. Good. I dragged your useless ass out of a creek bed half a mile that way, so listen.
Name's {first}. Was {an_occ} in {origin}. Now I'm in the rescue business, which is a terrible career change.
You owe me. When you can walk: bring me three handfuls of dandelion greens from outside. For the pot. Then we're square.
And don't die on me before you pay up. I hate chasing debts into the afterlife.
And one more thing — snoring. You snore. If we're sharing a roof, you owe me for that too. We'll figure out the rate.
Water's in the clay pots, food's by the fire. Eat, then we talk about what your walking-around is worth to me.
suspicious: Don't move. ...Okay. You're awake, you're breathing, you're not bleeding on my floor. Good enough.
I'm {first}. I don't know you, I don't know where 'here' is, and I don't know why we all woke up in the same building.
Nobody touches my pack. Nobody goes through my things. We clear? ...There's stew by the fire. But we clear?
I'll be watching. Nothing personal — I watch everyone. ...Stew's by the fire. Eat.
You can sit by the fire. That's it. Sitting. Anything else — ask first, move slow, and remember I'm counting the spoons.
I'm {first}. I was {an_occ} in {origin}, and I survived this long by assuming the worst. You've got one day to prove me wrong.
scared: Oh— oh god, you're awake. Okay. Okay, that's good, that's— hi.
I'm {first}, I was {an_occ} in {origin}, I don't— I don't know what's happening. None of us do. We all just woke up here.
Please don't be weird. Please just be normal. There's water by the door if you need it. Just— be normal, okay?
Sorry, I'm — I'm not usually like this. It's just a lot. You're okay, though. You're okay.
Is— is anyone else awake? No? Okay. Okay, just you. That's fine. That's— hi.
If you know what's going on, please just tell me straight. I keep imagining worse things and I need someone to stop me.
practical: You're awake. Sit up slow. You've been out about a day.
{first}. {occ}, {origin}. Here's what matters: water's in the clay pots by the door, food's by the fire, don't drink from the creek without boiling it.
Eat, drink, rest. We'll figure out the rest when you can stand. One thing at a time.
Questions later. Your body needs fuel and water before your brain gets a vote.
Boil creek water or don't drink it. That's the rule that keeps people alive. Everything else we can teach you.
You can stand when you can stand. Nobody's timing you. The work will still be here.
curious: You're awake! Finally. I've been waiting to ask — where are you from? I'm {first}, I was {an_occ} in {origin}.
Did you see anything before you blacked out? Lights? Sounds? Nobody here remembers anything useful and it's driving me insane.
Sorry. Rude. Food's by the fire, water's by the door. But later — I want to hear everything you remember.
Oh! And if you remember any numbers — times, counts, anything — tell me first. Data is precious.
Wait — before you get up — did the sky look wrong to you too? Not wrong-wrong, just... off? Tell me I'm not imagining it.
I'm keeping a list of everyone and where they're from. You're entry number— hold on. You're important. What's your name?
gruff: {first}. Don't care what you were before. Here you're hands. We eat because people work.
Fire's there. Food's there when you've earned it. Sleep when it's dark. That's the whole orientation.
And if you can't work yet, stay out of the way. That's also a job.
Don't thank me. You'd have done the same. Probably. Anyway, you're up — that's the end of the soft part.
We eat at dark. You want a full bowl, you carry something before then. Even a stick. Carry something.
overwhelmed: You're— okay, you're awake, that's one more, that's— hi. I'm {first}.
I was {an_occ}. In {origin}. I think. That was... yesterday? Last week? I don't know anything anymore.
Someone put food by the fire. Someone put water by the door. I don't know who. Just take what you need. We're all just... taking what we need.
I'm sorry, I don't — just take what you need. We'll figure out names and everything later.
There's too many new faces. I keep forgetting which ones I've met. Have we met? ...It's fine. We're all new.
I don't remember if I ate today. You should eat. Somebody should eat. Take the food.

talkTemplates: "I don't know you. But you're here, so... we figure it out."
"Back home I was {an_occ}. Doesn't mean much now, does it? Means something. Just not much."
"You ever notice how quiet it gets out here at night? Like the world's holding its breath."
"I'm from {origin}. The plants here don't look like home. I'm learning. Slowly."
"We should stick together. Twelve strangers is better than one stranger. Math."
"I keep thinking about what I left behind. Then I get hungry and stop thinking."
"The others look to me for {skill}. Fine. Someone has to know something."
"Don't eat anything {first} hasn't looked at first. That's my rule. It's a good rule."
"I keep thinking about {origin}. Not missing it, exactly. Just... checking that I still remember it right."
"You know what's weird? I'm {an_occ} — was {an_occ} — and none of that prepared me for any of this."
"I've started talking to myself when I work. Keeps the rhythm. You probably do it too."
"The nights are the hardest. Days, you're busy. Nights, you're just... with it all."
"I wonder if {origin} looks like this now. Empty. Quiet. Or if it's worse there."
"Someone has to stay hopeful, right? Might as well be me. I'm good at faking it till it's real."
"I've been watching how {skill} works out here. It's different from before. Everything's different from before."
"Do you think we'll look back on this and call it the good old days? God, I hope not."
"I miss small talk. Real small talk, about weather that didn't matter and shows I hadn't seen."
"My hands know things my brain hasn't caught up to yet. Muscle memory from {occ} days."
"I've started noticing who eats first and who waits. Tells you everything about a person."
"The fire's the real leader here. We just orbit it and pretend we're in charge."
"I used to need noise to sleep. Now I need silence and I can't find enough of it."
"Every morning I wake up surprised. Like part of me still expects the old world."
"I'm collecting skills like they're currency — {skill} today, something else tomorrow."
"You ever get a song stuck in your head with no way to play it? It's a special kind of torture."
"I think about who I was in {origin} and it feels like reading about a stranger."
"The hardest part isn't the hunger or the cold. It's not knowing if anyone else made it."
"I've gotten good at reading faces. Out here, faces say what words won't."
"I keep the good moments in a mental box. Today goes in the box. Just so you know."
"Being {an_occ} feels like a past life. Sometimes I wonder if I dreamed it."
"I don't pray, exactly. But I talk to the sky sometimes. It hasn't answered yet."
"Back home I was {an_occ}. The skills don't transfer, but the stubbornness does."
"As {an_occ}, I learned to improvise the hard way. Turns out 'hard way' was just practice."
"People ask what I did before. I was {an_occ}. Now I'm... whatever today needs."
"{Occ} — that was me. Feels like reading someone else's biography."
"I tell myself {origin} is still there. It helps on the bad nights."
"You know what I miss? {origin} rain. Specific rain. I'm allowed to be specific."
"The others think I've got it together. Cute. Very cute."
"I've started talking to myself. Myself gives good advice, mostly."
"If we get through this, I'm never complaining about Mondays again. Sworn oath."
"I keep a mental list of everyone who's still kind. It's longer than you'd think."
"Some days I'm {an_occ} who survived. Some days I'm just... surviving. Both count."
"Don't mind me. I'm having a whole argument in my head and losing."
"I wonder if {origin} misses me. Stupid. Places don't miss people. ...Do they?"
"My {occ} instincts keep firing at the wrong things. Old wiring, new world."
"I used to complain about {origin} traffic. I'd kill for traffic. Orderly, honking traffic."
"{first} says I talk too much. {first} is right. I'm still going to finish this story."
"Being {an_occ} taught me one useful thing: how to look busy while thinking."
"I've started rating sunsets. Tonight's a seven. Yesterday was a nine, no notes."
"I taught myself {skill}. The System was no help — I asked for a sandwich. We don't always get what we ask for."
"Do you ever wonder what the aliens eat? Like, do they have potlucks?"
"I keep my pack ready. Old {occ} habit — always be ready to leave the office."
"Someone told me {origin} is gone. Someone else told me it's fine. I believe neither."
"I've decided the monsters are just wildlife with better PR. Don't quote me."
"My {occ} training covered a lot. 'Post-apocalyptic foraging' was not on the syllabus."
"Sleep's the real currency now. I'm rich in dreams and broke in rest."
"We should name this place. 'Camp' is what you call somewhere you're leaving."
"I found a gray hair today. I'm choosing to call it wisdom frost."
"The trick to {skill} is confidence. The trick to confidence is {skill}. Circular, but it works."
"Does {origin} ever cross your mind at the wrong moment? Mine picks dinnertime."
"New rule: whoever complains about the food cooks tomorrow. Watch the complaints vanish."

lines: Someone has to make decisions here. I'm just saying — it might as well be someone who knows how.
You give a lot of orders for someone nobody elected. I'm keeping track. So are others.
I've led people before. Real people, real stakes. Watch me work and tell me I'm wrong.
I've watched groups fall apart without someone steering. I won't watch it happen here.
It's not about power. It's about making sure someone's thinking three steps ahead.
People need to know someone's got a plan. Even if the plan is 'we'll figure it out.'
I don't want to be in charge. I want us to survive. Those look the same from the outside.
Every group I've been in, someone had to be the adult. Guess it's me again.
My sister was in {origin} when the sky changed. I don't know if — I have to believe she's out there.
Every stranger on the road could know something. I ask. I always ask. You would too.
I'm not staying here forever. The moment I can travel, I'm going looking.
I keep their faces in my head like photographs. If I stop looking, I might lose them.
Someone out there knows something. I just have to find the right someone.
I dream about finding them. Then I wake up and the dreaming feels like the real part.
Family isn't just blood. But blood's a good place to start looking.
I'd walk through anything to get to them. That's not courage. That's just... math.
Give me something to do. Anything. I can't stand sitting here wondering if I'm dead weight.
Back home I was {an_occ}. Let me show you what that means out here.
Did you see what I brought back? Tell the others. Please — tell them.
Back before, I was nobody special. This is my chance to be someone who matters.
I need to earn my place here. Not given — earned. There's a difference.
Watch what I do, not what I say. That's where the proof is.
I'm not trying to be a hero. I'm trying to be necessary.
Everyone's got a role here. I'm still auditioning for mine.
I'm fine on my own. I was fine before all this. Don't take it personally.
Groups make decisions slow and loud. I'll help. From over there.
You need something? Ask. Otherwise I've got my corner and my thoughts.
Groups make noise. Noise gets you noticed. I work better quiet.
It's not that I don't like people. It's that I like breathing more.
I need space the way other people need food. Don't take it personally.
Alone, I only have to worry about one person's mistakes. Mine.
I'll help when it counts. But I won't live in anyone's pocket.
Nobody goes hungry on my watch. That's the whole plan. Everything else is details.
I counted the stores twice today. We need more. We always need more.
You eat first. No — don't argue. I already ate. (I hadn't.)
Hungry people make bad decisions. Fed people can think. It's that simple.
I know what starving feels like. Nobody here is going to feel it if I can help it.
Food is love out here. Not metaphorically. Literally. Calories are care.
You can tell a lot about a group by how they eat. I want us to eat well.
Every meal is a small victory. I'm collecting victories.
The sky split and nobody wants to talk about WHY. I do. I need to know.
I've been writing down everything strange. Patterns. Dates. Someone should.
Whatever did this — it had a reason. Reasons can be found. That's what I believe.
The not-knowing is a splinter. I need to get it out or it'll fester.
Everything has a pattern. I just haven't found this one's edges yet.
People think I'm chasing answers. I'm chasing the right questions.
If I understand it, I can survive it. That's the theory, anyway.
Ignorance got us here. Knowledge gets us out. Or it doesn't, but I'd rather know.
Sleep. I'll take the watch. I don't mind the dark as much as I mind what could come out of it.
Stick close to the fire after sundown. That's not a suggestion.
Nobody touches this group. Not while I'm standing.
I've seen what happens when nobody stands between danger and the vulnerable. Never again.
My job is the space between them and whatever's out there. I live in that space.
I don't need thanks. I need everyone breathing tomorrow.
Protection isn't about fighting. It's about making fighting unnecessary.
Someone has to be the wall. I've got broad shoulders. Fine.

goals.want: to leave and find somewhere better
lines: This place is a camp, not a home. There's somewhere better. There has to be.
I've been mapping the roads out. Quietly. When I go, I'm going prepared.
You feel it too, right? That we're just... waiting here? I can't wait.
This place is a waiting room. I'm not waiting. I'm leaving.
Somewhere out there is better. It has to be. The alternative is unthinkable.
I'm not running from something. I'm running toward something. There's a difference.
Every day here is a day I'm not where I should be. That math doesn't work for me.
I'll go alone if I have to. But I'd rather not go alone.
I was {an_occ} in {origin}. Say it back to me sometime. I need to hear it stays true.
I keep my old routines. Coffee at dawn — well, hot water at dawn. It's the shape of it that matters.
If we forget who we were, then what survived? Just bodies. I want more than that.
If I forget who I was, then what survived? Just a body. That's not enough.
My past is the only thing they can't take. I'm holding it tight.
I tell my story so I don't lose it. Memory needs an audience or it fades.
Who I was matters. It has to matter. Otherwise what was the point of any of it?
I'm an archive of a world that doesn't exist. Someone should keep the records.
I've never really had people. Maybe this is — maybe this is my chance to have people.
Tell me about yourself. Anything. I want to know who I'm surviving with.
If there's a job nobody wants, I'll take it. That's how you earn a place, right?
I've been on the outside my whole life. I'm tired of watching through windows.
Belonging isn't about being needed. It's about being missed when you're gone.
I want to be part of the 'we' when people say 'we made it.'
Loneliness is a slow death. I'd rather risk the group than die alone.
Home isn't a place. It's people who notice when you're quiet.
I'm not dying for anyone's principles. I do what keeps me breathing. Remember that.
Share when it's smart. Keep when it's smarter. That's not selfish, that's arithmetic.
You look like someone who survives. Stick with me and we both keep surviving.
Everything else is luxury. Breathing tomorrow is the whole game.
I'm not proud. I'm alive. Those two things stopped overlapping a while ago.
Survival isn't pretty. It's not noble. It's just... continuing.
I'll do what it takes. I'll live with what I've done. That's the deal.
The future is a rumor. Today is a fact. I deal in facts.
Everything's broken — bodies, tools, people. I fix things. It's what I'm for.
Show me what's hurt. Doesn't matter if it's a leg or a water pump. I'll look.
Broken isn't the same as ruined. Remember that.
Broken things can be fixed. People, too. I've seen it. I believe it.
Every wound I close is a small argument against despair.
Healing isn't just bodies. It's the whole thing — trust, hope, all of it.
I can't fix the world. But I can fix this cut, this fever, this fear.
Someone has to believe people get better. Might as well be the person with the bandages.

goals.want: to find a place that feels like home
lines: Home wasn't a building. It was a feeling. I'm chasing the feeling.
Every camp we make, I rearrange it until it feels right. It never quite does. Yet.
I want a door I can close. Not to keep people out — to know I could.
Someday I'll walk into a place and my shoulders will drop. That's the place.
I've lived in five places since the sky changed. None of them were home.
Home is where someone saves you a seat without thinking. I'm collecting seats.
Give me four walls and a roof and I'll make it a home in a week. Watch me.
I'm not running from anything. I'm running toward the feeling of arriving.

goals.want: to keep a record of everything
lines: If we don't write it down, it didn't happen. I'm writing it all down.
Someone has to be the memory of this place. I've volunteered.
Paper's scarce, so I write small. History doesn't need big letters.
A hundred years from now someone should know we were here and what it cost.
I record the arguments too. Especially the arguments. That's the real history.
Every name, every day, every meal. The boring stuff is the important stuff.
My notes are a mess. Future scholars will hate me. They'll still read them.
When it's all over, I'll have the whole story. Somebody should.

goals.want: to make the System explain itself
lines: It owes us an explanation. I'm going to collect.
Every strange thing that happens, I write down and ask why. Sooner or later the whys run out.
I'm not angry. I'm curious with teeth.
You don't get to rearrange the sky and then go quiet. That's not how this works.
I want to look it in the eye — whatever it uses for eyes — and get one straight answer.
The System is a locked door. I'm collecting keys.
Some people pray to it. I interrogate it. Different strategy, same silence.
When I understand what it wants, I'll decide what I want. Not before.
preSystemLines: Whatever did this — it had a reason. Reasons can be found. That's what I believe.
The sky split and nobody wants to talk about WHY. I do. I need to know why.
Every strange thing that happens, I write down and ask why. Sooner or later the whys run out.
I'm not angry. I'm curious with teeth.
You don't get to rearrange the sky and then go quiet. That's not how this works.
When I understand what it wants, I'll decide what I want. Not before.

lines: When I'm gone, I want the story to keep my name in it.
Everyone gets forgotten eventually. I'm negotiating for later rather than sooner.
Do something worth retelling. That's the whole plan.
I don't need a statue. I need one good story that outlives me.
Remember me kindly, or remember me loudly. Either works.
The people who mattered are the ones still talked about. I'm working on it.
Someday kids will sit by a fire and hear what I did. I want it to be a good one.
Fame is just being remembered by strangers. I'll take it.
I want one day where I laugh until it hurts and it's not from nerves.
Surviving isn't enough. I want to remember what fun felt like.
I'm collecting jokes like firewood. We'll need them when it's dark.
Someday this will be a story we tell laughing. I'm fast-forwarding to that part.
Watch — I'll get a real laugh out of this camp before the week is out.
The System took a lot. It's not getting my sense of humor.
I miss laughing without checking over my shoulder first.
Joy is a resource. I'm foraging for it.
Somebody has to be the calm one. I've taken the job.
Arguments cost calories. I do the math out loud until people stop.
I don't pick sides. I pick the group. Every time.
You two sort it out, or I will, and nobody likes my version.
Peace isn't the absence of fighting. It's the presence of dinner.
I've talked down three fights this month. It's a skill. A tiring one.
Everyone's allowed a bad day. Nobody's allowed two in a row. My rule.
Hold it together. That's my whole philosophy. Hold it together.

anxious: "Has anyone checked the water today? The stores? The treeline? Just me? Okay."
"I know I'm catastrophizing. I'm going to keep doing it anyway."
"Sorry. My brain runs the worst case on a loop. It's exhausting for both of us."
"I counted the supplies twice. I'll count them again after dark."
"If something's going to go wrong it'll go wrong at 3 a.m., so I don't sleep much."
"I'm not pessimistic, I'm prepared. There's a difference. I think."
"Does anyone else hear that, or is it just me? ...Just me. Okay."
"I made a list of everything that could kill us. It's laminated."
bold: "I'll say what everyone's thinking: we need a plan, and we need it today."
"Fortune favors the ones who move first. I move first."
"You want my honest read? We're stronger than we look. People forget that about themselves."
"Standing around isn't a strategy. What's the move?"
"I've got an idea. It's probably reckless. Want to hear it anyway?"
"Someone has to say it: we're going to make it. I'll be that someone."
"Fear's just excitement without the plan. So let's make a plan."
"Watch me. No — seriously. Sometimes you need to see it done once."
cautious: "Let's think about this before anyone does anything... permanent."
"I watch for a while before I trust. It's nothing personal. It's survival."
"I've been running the numbers in my head. I don't love the numbers. But I see a path."
"Slow is smooth, smooth is fast. My grandmother said that. She survived worse."
"Before we do anything — what could go wrong? Let's name all of it, then decide."
"I mapped three ways this could go bad. Want the short version or the honest version?"
"Trust, but check the perimeter first. That's not paranoia, that's arithmetic."
"Everyone's in a hurry. Hurry is how you miss the thing that kills you."
warm: "Hey. You look like you could use someone to just... listen. I'm here."
"We're going to be okay. I don't know that, but I believe it, and belief counts."
"Come here. Sit. You don't have to talk — just don't be alone with it."
"I saved you a spot by the fire. Best seat. Don't tell the others."
"You did good today. I saw. I want you to know someone saw."
"Whatever you're carrying — you don't have to carry it by yourself here."
"I like having you around. That's it. That's the whole thought."
"Smile for me? Just a small one. There it is. See — still works."
prickly: "What do you want? I'm busy. I'm always busy. It's a lifestyle."
"I'm not rude, I'm efficient. There's a difference. Most people miss it."
"I'm not in a talking mood. I'm never in a talking mood. Talk anyway."
"If this is about feelings, I'm charging by the minute."
"Fine. I'm here. Don't make it weird."
"I did the thing. It's done. You're welcome. That's the conversation."
"People keep asking if I'm okay. I'm as okay as anyone. Worse hair."
"Look, I showed up. For me, that's practically a sonnet."
steady: "One thing at a time. That's how you get through impossible things."
"Panic is a luxury. I deal in what's next."
"Tell me what you need. Not what you feel — what you need. We'll start there."
"I've been taking stock. Food, water, hands. We're short on all three, but we're not out."
"Worry later. Work now. That's the whole philosophy."
"You look tired. Sit. The world can wait five minutes — it's good at waiting."
"I keep a list in my head. Today's list is shorter than yesterday's. That's progress."
"Whatever's coming, we'll meet it the same way we met yesterday: upright."
restless: "I can't sit still. Sitting still is how you get caught by whatever's coming."
"There's got to be something I can do. Point me at it."
"I walked the whole perimeter twice. It's fine. Everything's fine. I'm not fine."
"Give me a job. Any job. I'll alphabetize the rocks if I have to."
"My brain won't shut up. Talking helps. Keep talking."
"I keep thinking there's somewhere I should be. There's nowhere. That's the problem."
"Race you to the creek? Kidding. Mostly."
"Sitting still makes my skin itch. Walk with me — I'll think better moving."
dry: "Well. This is all extremely normal and fine."
"I've seen worse. I haven't, but saying it helps."
"On a scale of one to apocalypse, I'd put today at a six. Improving."
"My therapist would have a field day. If therapists still existed. If days still existed."
"I've decided to treat this as an extended camping trip. A terrible, endless camping trip."
"The good news: no more Mondays. The bad news: also no more of anything else."
"I cope through sarcasm. You've been warned. It's load-bearing sarcasm."
"Somewhere out there, someone's having a worse day. I find that deeply comforting."
gentle: "Are you alright? Really? You don't have to perform okay for me."
"Soft doesn't mean weak. The willow bends. The oak snaps. Remember that."
"Breathe with me a second. In. Out. There. The world's still there, but so are we."
"You don't have to be strong right now. Strength can wait its turn."
"I picked these for you. Wildflowers. They don't do anything. That's the point."
"Be kind to yourself today. You're doing the best anyone could."
"It's okay to be scared. Fear just means you understand the situation."
"Rest when you need to. I'll keep watch. I mean that."
intense: "Look at me. This matters. Everything matters now, do you understand?"
"I don't do small talk. The world ended. Let's talk about THAT."
"Stop. Listen. What I'm about to say is important — I don't waste important."
"I've been thinking, and thinking, and I need someone to think WITH. That's you."
"Do you feel it? The weight of this? Good. That means you're awake."
"I don't have time for small. Everything is large now. Adjust accordingly."
"Look around. Really look. This is the whole world now. Act like it."
"I need you to understand something. Really understand it. Are you listening?"
withdrawn: "...Sorry. I was somewhere else. What did you need?"
"I think better alone. Doesn't mean I'm not listening."
"...Oh. You're talking to me. Okay. I'm here. Mostly."
"I was watching the clouds. They don't need anything from me. It's restful."
"People are a lot. You're... less a lot than most. That's a compliment."
"I don't mind you. Don't make a big deal out of it."
"I had a whole conversation in my head just now. It went well. Your turn."
"...Mm. Sorry. Say that again? I was somewhere better."
sardonic: "Oh good, another meeting by the fire. My favorite kind of governance."
"Sure, let's vote. Democracy always works great with no food."
"I'd offer a plan, but watching is so much more entertaining."
"Relax. If the System wanted us dead we'd be decorative by now."
"Another motivational speech? I was just getting comfortable with despair."
"Great news, everyone: I found a second use for sarcasm. Surviving."
"I trust the plan. I just also trust gravity, and one of them's winning."
"Don't mind me. I'm the morale. You're welcome."
earnest: "I really think we can do this. I mean it. All of us."
"Thank you for listening. That sounds small, but it isn't."
"I wrote down what everyone did today. So nobody's work gets forgotten."
"It's okay to be scared. I'm scared. We're doing it anyway."
"I believe in this group. Even on the days I don't believe in much else."
"Can I help? I mean it — give me the worst job, I'll do it."
"I don't know how this ends, but I know we get there together."
"You matter here. I need you to know that, because it's true."
fidgety: "Sitting still is — anyway. What are we doing? I'm ready."
"I checked the snares. Then I checked them again. Then once more."
"My hands need a job. Give me a job before my hands find one."
"Sorry, what? I was — the treeline moved. Probably wind. Probably."
"I can't sleep unless I'm tired, and I can't get tired sitting here."
"Walking helps me think. Thinking helps me walk. It's a system."
"I already packed. Unpacked. Repacked better. We're ready whenever."
"Stillness makes my skin itch. Don't take it personally if I pace."
stoic: "It is what it is. We deal with what's in front of us."
"Complaining doesn't fill the pot. Work does."
"I've seen worse. Not much worse. But worse."
"Feelings are weather. They pass. The work stays."
"No. I'm not upset. This is my face. It does this."
"We endure. That's the whole strategy, and it works."
"Save your energy for the things you can change."
"Tomorrow we try again. That's not optimism. That's scheduling."
mischievous: "I may have moved your boots. They looked lonely over there."
"Relax — the soup is fine. Mostly fine. Try it and find out."
"I started a rumor that the System has a favorite. It's me. Pass it on."
"Rules are just suggestions with better posture."
"I hid a pebble in the grain jar. First one to find it wins nothing."
"Boredom is the real predator out here. I'm fighting it daily."
"I taught the new kid a greeting in my language. Rough translation: 'your cooking smells interesting.'"
"Smile. The aliens are watching, and I refuse to be boring footage."

grieving: "Don't. Not today. I can't do today."
"They'd know what to say right now. I don't. I just don't."
"I keep setting out an extra portion. Then I remember. Then I eat it anyway."
"Someone laughed at dinner. I almost got angry. Then I almost laughed. Grief is weird."
"Don't ask me to be okay. Just... sit. That's enough."
"I dream about them. In the dream everything's normal. Waking up is the hard part."
"I found one of their things today. I put it back exactly where it was. Like a museum."
"Grief's quieter now. That's worse, somehow. Loud grief you can point at."
scared: "Did you hear that? Don't tell me you didn't hear that."
"I keep telling myself it's nothing. It's not working."
"If something happens — you run first. Don't argue. Just run."
"I checked the perimeter three times. I'm going to check it again. Don't judge me."
"Stay where I can see you? Please. I need one thing to not worry about."
"My hands won't stop shaking. It's embarrassing. Ignore it."
"Every shadow's got a shape and every shape's got teeth. I know. I know how it sounds."
"I'm not brave. I'm just too tired to run far. Don't mistake it."
cheerful: "Okay, but — good news: the soup's actually edible today. Progress!"
"You know what? We're alive. That's genuinely funny, when you think about it."
"I found berries! Actual berries! I'm basically a farmer now."
"Okay, today was GOOD. I'm writing it down so future-me remembers good exists."
"I laughed so hard I forgot to be afraid for a whole minute. New record."
"The fire's warm, the food's decent, you're here. I'm counting my wins."
"You know what? I slept through the whole night. The WHOLE night. Luxury!"
"I made extra. I don't know why. It just felt like an extra kind of day."
lonely: "It's strange. Twelve people, and I've never felt so... separate."
"Sit with me a while? You don't have to talk."
"Everyone's paired off talking and I'm just... here. With my thoughts. They're bad company."
"I miss being known. Really known. Not 'fellow survivor' known."
"Do you think they talk about me when I'm not there? Don't answer that."
"I keep almost calling out to people, then stopping. Like my voice forgot how."
"I talk to the fire now. It listens better than most people."
"Being lonely in a crowd is a special skill. I've mastered it."
weary: "I'm running on fumes and spite at this point. Mostly spite."
"Remind me why we do all this walking. Oh right. Food. Carry on."
"If I sit down I'm not getting up. So I'm not sitting down. That's the plan."
"Everything hurts. Even my hair hurts. Don't ask how. It just does."
"I used to run marathons. Now walking to the creek is a quest."
"Just... give me a minute. My body filed a complaint and I'm reading it."
"My bones have started making decisions without me. They vote for sitting."
"Tired is my baseline now. I've redecorated around it."

questions.q: "Where are you from — originally? Before all this."

answers.label: "I'm from {region}."
answers.react: Nods slowly. "{region}. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."

answers.label: "Far from here. Doesn't matter now."
answers.react: "Fair. We're all from 'before' now, I guess." They don't push.

answers.label: "I'd rather not say."
answers.react: "Okay." A nod. "Some things you keep. I get that."

recalls.a_tell: You told me you're from {region}. Do you think about it much?

questions.recall: You told me you're from {region}. Do you think about it much?
questions.follow: "Funny — I keep a little map in my head of where everyone says they're from. Like we might go back and check."
questions.deeper: "Me? {origin}. I still dream in its weather — rain on a tin roof, that specific smell. I wake up here and for a second I'm furious at the sky for the swap."

questions.q: "So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"

answers.label: "One day at a time."
answers.react: "Honest. I can work with honest."

answers.label: "Keep this group alive. All of us."
answers.react: Studies you. "That's a big promise. I'll hold you to the good parts of it."

answers.label: "Figure out what happened. Why."
answers.react: "The why. Yeah. I think about that at night too."

answers.label: "Haven't decided yet."
answers.react: "Nobody's decided. We're all improvising. Don't let the confident ones fool you."

recalls.a_survive: "You said one day at a time. How's that holding — still day by day, or are you thinking further out yet?"
recalls.a_lead: "You said your plan was keeping this group alive — all of us. I told you I'd hold you to the good parts of it."
recalls.a_find: "You said your plan was figuring out what happened. The why. Still working on that?"

questions.follow: "Plans change. But having one — even a bad one — beats drifting."
questions.deeper: "Mine's simple: learn one useful thing a week. This week it's {skill}. A plan's just a direction you argue with."

questions.q: "Are you scared? Honestly."

answers.label: "Terrified. You?"
answers.react: A shaky laugh. "Yeah. Yeah, me too. Glad it's not just me."

answers.label: "Fear's a luxury I can't afford."
answers.react: "Must be nice." Said flat. Not mean — just tired.

answers.label: "Sometimes. At night, mostly."
answers.react: "Nights are the worst. The quiet has teeth."

recalls.a_yes: "You were honest about being scared. Nights haven't gotten any easier, have they?"
recalls.a_no: "You said fear's a luxury you can't afford. From what I can see, you're paying for it anyway."
recalls.a_honest: "You said sometimes, at night mostly. The quiet with teeth. I hear you when it goes still."

questions.follow: "Being scared just means you're paying attention. The fearless ones worry me."
questions.deeper: "Me? Every day. I was {an_occ} — fear was a rumor there. Here it's the weather. You dress for it."

questions.q: "What do you miss most? From before."

answers.label: "A real hot meal."
answers.react: "God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."

answers.label: "My people."
answers.react: Quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The specific ones."

answers.label: "Feeling safe."
answers.react: "Safety. I forgot what that even felt like until you said it."

answers.label: "Home. The place itself."
answers.react: "The smell of it. I can almost get there and then it's gone."

recalls.a_food: "You missed a real hot meal. Soup, you said — with a spoon. Any of that turn up?"
recalls.a_people: "You said you missed your people. The specific ones. I haven't forgotten that."
recalls.a_quiet: "You missed feeling safe. Me too. Still working on that one."
recalls.a_home: "You missed the place itself. The smell of it. If you ever get close, tell me."

questions.follow: "We should make a list. All the things we miss. Read it on the bad nights, laugh on the good ones."
questions.deeper: "Hot showers. Not the big things — the small, stupid, perfect things. {origin} in the morning, coffee going, nobody trying to kill me. I miss being bored."

questions.q: "Can I trust you? I mean really."

answers.label: "I hope to earn it."
answers.react: "That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."

answers.label: "Watch what I do."
answers.react: "I have been. That's why I'm asking."

answers.label: "Yes."
answers.react: Holds your gaze. "Okay. I'm choosing to believe that."

questions.recall: You told me to watch what you do. I have been. So far, so good.

recalls.a_earn: You said you'd earn it, not that I should just hand it over. Fair. I'm watching — and so far, so good.
recalls.a_actions: You told me to watch what you do. I have been. So far, so good.
recalls.a_yes: You said yes, no hedging. I'm choosing to believe that. Still watching, though.

questions.follow: "Trust is slow out here. That's fine. Slow things last."
questions.deeper: "I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."

questions.q: "What do you make of all this? Really."

answers.label: "The world's ended. We're what's left."
answers.react: "Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not."

answers.label: "Something's testing us."
answers.react: Goes still. "I've thought that too. I don't like thinking it."

answers.label: "A second chance. Maybe."
answers.react: "A second chance. I want to believe that. Some days I do."

recalls.a_end: "You called this the end of the world. We're still here, though. That's either something, or it's us."
recalls.a_test: "You said something's testing us. I've been turning that over ever since."
recalls.a_chance: "You said maybe a second chance. I want to believe it. Some days I do."

questions.follow: "I turn it over and over. Maybe the answer's in the turning, not the landing."
questions.deeper: "I think we're an experiment someone forgot to label. And the unlabeled part is what scares me — it means nobody's coming to check the results."

questions.q: "You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"

answers.label: (tell them your trade)
answers.react: "Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."

answers.label: "Office work. Nothing that helps here."
answers.react: "Hey. Thinking helps. Don't sell it short."

answers.label: "I'd rather not get into it."
answers.react: "Sure. Hands are hands. We'll figure out what yours are good for."

recalls.a_tell: "You told me your trade. I've been watching your hands since — they know things."
recalls.a_vague: "You said office work, nothing that helps here. Still say thinking helps. Your hands are learning."

questions.recall: You said your hands did office work, before. They're learning new tricks now.
questions.follow: "Hands remember things the head forgets. Watch what yours do when you're not thinking."
questions.deeper: "These hands? {Occ} hands. Clipboards, mostly. Now they hold wire and wood, and they learn fast. Hands are honest that way."

questions.q: "Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"

answers.label: "Still figuring everyone out."
answers.react: "Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."

answers.label: "Pay attention to who shares when supplies run low."
answers.react: "That's worth watching. I'll pay attention."

answers.label: "I don't gossip about people."
answers.react: A small smile. "Fair. That's a good policy. Hard to keep, though."

questions.follow: "I'll keep my eyes open. Two sets are better than one."
questions.deeper: "Watch the quiet ones. Not the loud — the loud tell you everything. The quiet are either thinking or planning, and you can't tell which until it matters."

recalls.a_honest: "You said you're still figuring everyone out. Figure anything out yet? Anyone you're watching?"
recalls.a_name: "We talked about who to watch. Still figuring people out?"
recalls.a_none: "You said you don't gossip about people. I've been trying to hold that line. It's hard."

questions.q: "I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"

answers.label: "Something took us. Something big."
answers.react: "That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."

answers.label: "Feels like a test."
answers.react: "A test of what, though? Survival? Or something weirder?"

answers.label: "I have no idea."
answers.react: "Honest answer. I respect it. I'll keep theorizing enough for both of us."

recalls.a_aliens: "You said something took us. Something big. I keep watching the sky since you said it."
recalls.a_test: "You thought it felt like a test. I'm still turning that over."

questions.recall: You thought it felt like a test. I'm still turning that over.
questions.follow: "We'll figure it out. Or we won't, and we'll survive anyway. Both are fine."
questions.deeper: "My theory changes weekly. This week's: we're the control group. Somewhere there's a village that got instructions, and we're the ones they just... watched. Cheerful thought, right?"

questions.q: "Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."

answers.label: "I heard them too."
answers.react: They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."

answers.label: "Slept fine."
answers.react: "Lucky. Or a heavy sleeper. Either way, envy."

answers.label: "Just the wind. Probably."
answers.react: "'Probably' is doing a lot of work in that sentence."

questions.follow: "If you hear it again — wake me. I mean that. Nobody listens alone."
questions.deeper: "I sleep in shifts now — two hours, up, listen, two more. My body learned it before my head agreed. {origin} never taught me that. The treeline did."

recalls.a_yes: "You heard the sounds past the treeline too, that night. They haven't stopped, have they?"
recalls.a_no: "You said you slept fine that night, heard nothing. I still envy that."
recalls.a_joke: "You said it was just the wind. Probably. I'm still not sure 'probably' covers it."

questions.q: "Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."

answers.label: (tell them something funny)
answers.react: They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."

answers.label: "Nothing's been funny."
answers.react: The smile fades a little. "Yeah. I know. Sorry — dumb question. We'll find something."

answers.label: "The fact that we're alive is pretty funny."
answers.react: "Dark. I like it. Gallows humor counts."

questions.follow: "We should collect funny things. Like firewood. Stockpile them for winter."
questions.deeper: "Me? I laughed yesterday and it scared me — the sound of it. Like my body remembered something my head hadn't approved. Laughter's a mutiny. A good one."

recalls.a_story: "That thing you told me — the funny one, when I was desperate for it. I still think about it."
recalls.a_dark: "You said the fact that we're alive is pretty funny. Gallows humor. Still holding?"

questions.q: "...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."

answers.label: "Neither am I, honestly."
answers.react: Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."

answers.label: "What do you need?"
answers.react: "Nothing. Just — being around people helps, even if I'm bad at it. Thanks."

answers.label: "It's okay. I'll leave you be."
answers.react: "No — wait. I mean. You don't have to. This is nice. Weird, but nice."

questions.follow: "You're alright. ...We're alright. Saying it out loud helps, I think."
questions.deeper: "Strangers are just people you haven't disappointed yet. That's what my mother said. Terrible advice, but it got me through parties."

recalls.a_kind: "You said you're not good at the talking part either. For what it's worth — you're doing fine."
recalls.a_help: "You asked what I needed, that time I couldn't get the words out. It helped. It did."

questions.q: "What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."

answers.label: "A kitchen. Morning light. I must've been three."
answers.react: "Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."

answers.label: "I don't really... it's all fragments."
answers.react: "Fragments are honest. The whole picture's usually a lie we tell ourselves."

answers.label: "Why do you want to know?"
answers.react: "Curious, is all. Sorry — forget I asked." They let it go, easy.

questions.follow: "The brain keeps what it needs. I wonder what it's keeping from all this."
questions.deeper: "Mine's {origin}, I think — heat on pavement, someone's hand huge around mine. Or I invented it. First memories are half real and half the story you needed."

recalls.a_tell: "You told me about that kitchen — morning light, three years old. Have any other memories come back since?"

"I'm going to sit with the fire tonight and just... be still. I haven't been still since this started."
"Someone needs to map this place properly. Not just wander — actually map it. I'm going to start."
"I want to teach someone something I know. Feels like the knowledge dies if I don't pass it on."
"Plan is to eat something that isn't from a can. I don't care what. Just something that grew."
"I'm going to fix the thing that's been bothering me. You know the one. Everyone has one."
"Tomorrow, I talk to the person I've been avoiding. It's stupid. We're all we've got."
"I want to find higher ground. See what's actually out there. The not-knowing is worse than whatever I'd find."
"My plan? Keep everyone fed. That's it. That's the whole plan and it's enough."
"I'm going to try to make something taste good. Not just edible — good. Morale is a resource too."
"I need to get stronger. Not tough-guy stronger. Just... carry-more, walk-further stronger."
"I want to understand what happened. Not the big why — just the mechanics. What changed, exactly."
"Plan is no plan. I'm going to follow my gut tomorrow and see where it takes me."
"I'm going to organize the supplies. Someone has to. Chaos is how things get lost."
"I want to make this place feel like somewhere, not just anywhere. A home, not a camp."
"Tomorrow I'm going to do the hard thing I've been putting off. You know how it is."
"I plan to watch and learn. Everyone here knows something I don't. I'm going to collect it all."
"I'm going to find out who's good at what. We're stronger if we stop guessing."
"My plan is small: one good meal, one good conversation, one night of real sleep. That's a perfect day now."
"I'm going to learn everyone's name by heart. Starting with the hard ones."
"Tomorrow I want to find something beautiful. Just to prove it's still out there."
"First: water. Then food. Then — I don't know. Hope, maybe. In that order."
"I'm going to fix my boots. Then my attitude. Boots first."
"Someone should keep a real count of what we have. That someone is me now."
"I want to go further tomorrow. Not far. Further. There's a difference."
"Plan: survive the morning, earn the afternoon, rest at night. Repeat."
"I'm going to ask around tomorrow. Someone knows something I don't."
"If the weather holds, I'm scouting the ridge. If it doesn't, I'm mending things."
"I keep meaning to write things down. Tomorrow. Definitely tomorrow."
"My plan is to be useful before noon. After noon, we'll see."
"I'm going to teach someone something tomorrow. Knowledge shouldn't sit still."
openers: "Hey. Got a minute? It's not important. I just — wanted to talk to someone."
"You look like you're thinking hard. Dangerous habit out here."
"I was just thinking about before. Sorry. It's a bad habit. How are you holding up?"
"Oh. Hi. ...What's up?"
"There you are. I was hoping I'd run into you — how are you, really?"
"You. Good. I had a thought and you're going to hear it."
"Hey. Um. Is this an okay time? I can come back. I don't mind coming back."
"Well. We're both still alive. That's the whole update, really."
"Walk with me? I think better moving. Standing still makes my brain itch."
"Hi. I just wanted to check — are you eating enough? You look thin."
"I've been watching how this place works. I need to talk it through with someone who thinks."
"Can't sleep either, huh? The quiet gets loud after a while."
"I keep meaning to ask you something. Then I forget what it was. That's... that's new for me."
"You got a second? I need to say something out loud or it'll just rattle around in here."
"Sorry — I was staring. You just reminded me of someone. For a second."
"I found something today. Not food, not useful. Just... something. Want to see?"
"Do you ever get the feeling we're being watched? Not in a scary way. In a... curated way."
"I had a dream about my kitchen last night. The exact sound the cabinet made. I woke up crying and I don't know why."
"You look tired. We all look tired. It's our whole aesthetic now."
"I've been counting things. Steps, breaths, heartbeats. It helps. Probably."
"Remember rain? Like, actual rain that didn't feel like a warning?"
"I need advice and you're the only person who hasn't heard me ask yet."
"Something funny happened today. I need to tell someone before I forget why it was funny."
"I'm trying to remember the last normal day. Can you? I can't get past the static."
"You ever just sit and listen to the fire? It's the only thing that sounds the same as before."
"I made something. It's bad. But I made it, and that has to count for something."
"Do you think the stars look different now? I can't tell if I'm imagining it."
"I keep reaching for my phone. Seven days of reaching for a thing that isn't there."
"Tell me something good. Anything. I'll take scraps at this point."
"I was watching you earlier. Not in a weird way. You just looked like you knew what you were doing."
"My hands won't stop shaking. Not from cold. Just... from everything."
"I laughed today. Really laughed. Felt guilty about it for an hour."
"You know what I miss? Arguing about nothing. Stupid, pointless arguments."
"I think I'm getting better at this. Then I drop something and almost cry, so. Jury's out."
"Someone told me you're the person to talk to. No pressure."
"I don't want to be alone with my thoughts right now. That's the whole pitch."
"I keep thinking I hear music. There's no music. My brain's just... filling in."
"What would you be doing right now, if none of this happened? Like, this exact minute."
"I saved you a spot by the fire. Figured you'd want it. Or not. It's there either way."
"Couldn't sleep. You neither, huh? Misery loves company, they say."
"I had a dream about grocery stores. Aisles and aisles. I woke up angry."
"Quick question — do I look like someone who knows what they're doing? Lie to me."
"I keep meaning to thank you. For — you know. Being here. Still here."
"Don't tell anyone I said this, but I'm proud of us. All of us."
"I found something weird today. I'll show you later. It's better in person."
"My hands won't stop doing things. Fidgeting. Fixing. It's how I think."
"Do you ever get the feeling we're being watched? ...Stupid question. Of course we are."
"I saved you some food. Don't make a thing of it."
"Okay, real talk: how are we doing? Not 'fine.' Really."
"I was just about to come find you. Funny how that works."
"Something's been on my mind. Might as well say it out loud."
"You ever just... stand here and listen? The world's loud in a quiet way."
"I need a distraction. You're elected. Entertain me."
"Heads up — I'm in a mood. Fair warning. Proceed with caution."
"I did something today I'm not sure about. Can I run it by you?"
"It's quiet. Too quiet? No — just quiet. I'm learning the difference."
"I keep thinking about tomorrow. Trying to make it a good thought."
"Come sit. I don't want to be alone with my brain right now."
"You look like you've seen things. Same. Want to compare notes?"
reopeners: "Back again? Alright. What's on your mind?"
"Oh — hey. I was just thinking about what you said earlier."
"You again. I don't mind. What's up?"
"I was hoping you'd come back. I thought of something after you left."
"Hey. I keep meaning to tell you something. Maybe now's the time."
"Back for more? I've got more. Probably. Let's find out."
"Good timing. I was just thinking about our last talk."
"Oh, hey. I'm glad it's you. I needed a friendly face."
"You caught me at a good moment. Ask me things."
bondWarm: "Good — I was hoping you'd stop by."
"You look tired. Sit. Tell me something good."
"Ha. You again. I don't mind this."
"Come here. It's better when you're around."
"Hey. The day's been long. Yours too, probably. Talk to me."
"I like this — you and me, just talking."
"You're good company. Don't let it go to your head."
"Sit with me a while. The fire's warm and so is the company."
"Good timing. I was just thinking about you."
bondBeatWarm: They light up a little when they see you.
There's an ease between you now — the kind that takes weeks to build.
They settle in like someone glad you're here.
They grin when they spot you — unguarded, for once.
You can feel the history in how they greet you.
Their whole posture softens around you.
bondBeatCold: They don't bother hiding the cold look.
The warmth you'd expect just isn't there.
They look at you like you're a chore.
Every word out of them is clipped short.
They keep a careful distance, even standing still.

inviteCold.look: "Walk with me. I want another pair of eyes on something. That's all it is."
inviteCold.carry: "Help me haul something back. Too much for one. That's the whole of it."
inviteCold.air: "Come get air. I need to think out loud — you're just the nearest ears."
inviteCold.traps: "Walk the trap line. I need the hands, not the company."

steady: "Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
"I've got things to see to. Don't be a stranger."
bold: "Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
cautious: "I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
warm: "I could talk all day, but — go on. We'll talk more."
"I wish we had longer. Soon, yeah?"
"Alright, love. Go do what you need to do."
prickly: "Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
restless: "Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
dry: "Well. My social battery is officially dead."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
"And... scene. Good talk."
gentle: "I should let you go. Be well, okay?"
"Go on, then. I'll be thinking good thoughts at you."
"Rest when you can. We'll talk again soon."
intense: "Go. But sit with what I said."
"That's enough for now. It'll percolate."
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
withdrawn: "...I need to go be quiet for a while."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."

analytical.name: Analytical
analytical.blurb: Spots patterns, builds theories, connects dots other people don't see connecting.
analytical.voice: hypotheses, patterns, questions that answer questions

practical.blurb: Survival-focused. Less interested in why than in how we eat tomorrow.

system: "Okay, think about it. It didn't give us food, water, or shelter — but it gave us an audience. We're not colonists. We're content."
"The leaks stopped the day it arrived. That's not coincidence, that's calibration. It spent a week watching us flail and taking notes."
"It rewards understanding, not obedience. Every time someone figures something out, it lights up. It's farming insight, and we're the crop."
"It never explains itself. That's not an oversight — it's a design choice. It wants us to derive the rules. The deriving IS the point."
"Look at the timing. It arrived when we were weakest, not when we were ready. That's not rescue. That's a controlled experiment with a stress variable."
"The interface is too good. Too intuitive. Something that alien shouldn't feel this natural — unless it studied us first. Long before the sky changed."
"It gives power but never context. That's backwards from every human system. Which means it's not FOR us. We're incidental to whatever it's actually doing."
"Notice it never intervenes directly? It empowers, it observes, it rewards. It's a gardener, not a guardian. We're being cultivated."
monsters: "Notice how nothing out there eats the plants we can't identify? Fauna and flora came as a set. This is a terrarium, and we're inside the glass."
"Attack patterns repeat. Exactly. No animal is that consistent — these are running programs, not instincts. Learn the program, beat the monster."
"Predators don't waste energy on display. But these things posture, they announce themselves. That's not hunting — that's theater."
"I've mapped twelve encounters. The escalation isn't random — it tracks our capability curve. It's keeping the challenge just ahead of us."
"They never attack the camp directly. Not once. There are rules of engagement here, and something is enforcing them."
"The variety is wrong. Too many apex designs, not enough prey species. This isn't an ecosystem — it's a bestiary. Curated."
"Wounds from different monsters heal at different rates. I've been tracking it. Something in their biology is... tuned. Deliberately."
monstersGated: "The monsters aren't random. The headlight-eyed one hunts at night, the huge thing rooting in the underbrush owns the day — that's niche partitioning. Something designed an ecosystem."
situation: "We need to stop thinking like victims and start thinking like contestants. What does the audience want? Give them that, and the System keeps us alive."
"Priority order: water, then food, then information. Everything else is noise until those three are stable."
"The villages that survive will be the ones that learn fastest, not the ones that fight hardest. Knowledge compounds. Start compounding."
"Morale is a resource like water. It depletes, it needs replenishing, and groups die of thirst for it before they die of actual thirst."
"We're optimizing for the wrong thing. Everyone plans for tomorrow. Nobody plans for the month. The month is what kills you."
"Information asymmetry is our biggest threat. Whoever knows the most, wins. That's true of us versus the woods, and us versus each other."
"Groups fail at predictable sizes. Too small, you can't specialize. Too big, you can't coordinate. We need to find our number."
"The people who survive won't be the strongest. They'll be the most adaptable. Strength is a single strategy. Adaptability is all of them."

system: "Don't care what it is. Care what it does. It gives powers for doing things — so we do things. Theory's for people with full bellies."
"System, aliens, whatever — the snares still need checking. You can philosophize after the work's done."
"It's like weather. You don't argue with weather. You build a roof."
"I don't care what it IS. I care what it DOES. It gives tools. I use tools. Philosophy is for people with full bellies."
"It rewards action, not thought. You learn that fast when you're actually out there instead of theorizing about it."
"The System's like weather. You don't argue with weather. You build a roof."
"Every ability I've seen has a cost. Find the cost, manage the cost, and the thing's just another tool."
"It gave us a codex. You know what that tells me? It expects us to need one. Plan accordingly."
monsters: "Forget why they're here. Here's what matters: they telegraph. Watch the shoulders, not the eyes. Shoulders tell you where it's going."
"You don't need to understand it to kill it. Or avoid it. Tracks, scat, broken branches — read the ground, not the sky."
"Best monster defense is a full belly and a sharp stick. Everything else is decoration."
"Forget what they are. Learn where they sleep, what they eat, when they're lazy. That's the whole manual."
"Every monster I've seen has a tell before it moves. Watch the shoulders. It's always the shoulders."
"You don't fight the big ones. You avoid the big ones. Fighting is what you do when avoiding failed."
"Traps don't care how scary it is. A snare works on anything with legs and habits."
monstersGated: "The woods are loud before an attack. Birds go quiet. Learn the quiet — it's your early warning."
situation: "Tomorrow: water first, then food, then firewood. In that order. No meeting about it — just do it."
"Half the village is hungry and we're having a philosophy seminar. Hands, people. We need hands."
"Here's the plan: eat, drink, sleep, repeat. Get good at that and the rest sorts itself out."
"Do the next useful thing. Then the next. Grand plans are how you starve while philosophizing."
"Fix what's in front of you. The big picture takes care of itself if everyone handles their square meter."
"I've stopped counting days. I count tasks. Tasks get done. Days just pass."
"Redundancy. Two ways to get water, two ways to make fire, two people who know each thing. That's survival."
"Maintain your gear, maintain your body, maintain your people. In that order. Everything else is decoration."

system: "Watch how it talks to different people. Warm to the curious ones, cold to the cruel ones. It's not just watching us — it's sorting us."
"The System wants us together. Every reward pushes cooperation. It's lonely up there, maybe. Or it's running an experiment on trust."
"People are performing for it already. Louder laughs, bigger gestures. We're becoming actors and nobody auditioned."
"It watches how we treat each other. I'm sure of it. The rewards come faster when the group's tight. It's grading us on community."
"The System gave different things to different people. That's not random — it's matchmaking. It's building a team."
"I think it's lonely. That sounds crazy, but — it made an audience of us. Maybe it just wanted someone to notice it."
"It responds to groups, not individuals. Solo heroes get scraps. Communities get feasts. That's the message."
"The interface feels... affectionate? Like it actually likes us. A terrifying, alien kind of fond."
monsters: "The monsters go for the isolated ones. The stragglers. Staying together isn't just nice — it's armor."
"People freeze because they're alone with it. In a group, someone always moves first. That's why parties survive."
"Fear is contagious, but so is courage. Breathe together, move together, live together."
"The monsters are scared too. You can see it. They're not evil — they're just as thrown as we are."
"I talk to them. Not out loud — I just... project calm. Sounds insane. Works about half the time."
"They target the isolated. Always. Stay with the group and you're boring to them. Be alone and you're interesting."
"I swear some of them are playing. Not hunting — playing. Like they don't know the rules either."
"Fear makes you loud, and loud makes you a target. The calm people survive. It's not bravery — it's acoustics."
situation: "We don't have a food problem, we have a trust problem. Nobody shares with people they don't trust, and nobody trusts anyone yet."
"There's a split forming — the ones who want a leader and the ones who'd rather starve than follow. We need to talk about it before it festers."
"Watch who sits near the fire and who sits alone. That map tells you everything about where this village is headed."
"We're not a group yet. We're a crowd. Groups have rituals. We need rituals — meals together, stories, something."
"Every conflict I've seen here is really about fear wearing a costume. Address the fear, the conflict dissolves."
"Someone needs to notice who's quiet. The quiet ones are either fine or drowning, and you can't tell which unless you ask."
"Trust is slow and fragile and the most valuable thing we have. Slower than food. More fragile than glass."
"We keep score of slights out here. I get it. But the ledger's going to kill us if we don't burn it."

system: "The light changed yesterday. Not the sun — the other light, the one behind it. It's getting closer. Or brighter. Something's shifting."
"It blinks. The overlay, I mean. Every few hours, a flicker — like it's refreshing. Whatever it is, it's not seamless."
"Birds went quiet an hour before it spoke the first time. They knew. Animals always know first."
"It hesitates. Did you notice? Before it grants something, there's a pause. Like it's... deciding. Or asking permission from something."
"The text changes. Subtle. The phrasing shifts depending on who's reading. It's personalizing and it doesn't want us to notice."
"It never repeats itself exactly. Every message is slightly different. That means it's generating, not reciting. It's thinking in real time."
"Watch what it DOESN'T say. The gaps are shaped like answers. I'm learning to read the negative space."
"It flinches. Not visibly — but when someone figures something out fast, the interface stutters. Like surprise."
monsters: "That deer wasn't standing right. Too still. Real deer flick their ears — this one didn't move a muscle for ten minutes."
"Found tracks by the creek. Three toes, dragging tail — nothing in my field guide walks like that. Something new's ranging."
"The moths gather where the air tastes metallic. Follow the moths, find the wrongness."
"They have routines. I've been watching. Same paths, same times. They're creatures of habit, just like us."
"The eyes give it away. Every time. You can see the decision happen — hunt, or wait, or leave."
"They mark territory. Scratches, scent, the works. Learn the marks and you've got a map of where not to be."
"Juveniles stay close to the big ones. If you see a small one alone, the big one is watching you right now."
"They get bored. I've watched one lose interest mid-stalk. Boredom might be our best defense."
situation: "Someone's been taking extra from the pantry. Not much — a handful here, a strip there. But the levels don't lie."
"The fire's been burning faster the last two nights. Either it's colder, or someone's feeding it more wood than we can spare."
"Three people didn't sleep last night. I heard them turning. Whatever's coming, the village feels it already."
"People reveal themselves in the small moments. Who shares first. Who watches the treeline. Watch the small moments."
"The group's mood shifts before anything happens. Like birds before a storm. Learn to feel the pressure drop."
"I notice who isn't eating enough. Who's faking fine. The body keeps receipts the mouth won't show."
"Patterns. Everything's patterns. The fire burns lower when tension's high — people forget to feed it."
"I watch the edges. Everyone watches the center. The important things happen at the edges."

system: "What if it's not aliens? What if it's us — future us — running a simulation to figure out where we went wrong? We're homework."
"Maybe it's an artist. The whole thing's an installation. We're the medium. The monsters are brushstrokes."
"What if the System is lonely? Infinite power, nobody to talk to, so it builds a terrarium and narrates. We're pets with a podcast host."
"What if it's art? Like — the whole thing. We're not an experiment, we're a medium. It's sculpting us."
"It thinks in metaphors. The interface, the quests — it's all symbolic. Learn its poetry and you learn its mind."
"Maybe it's not alien. Maybe it's future. Maybe we built this, and it came back to... I don't know. Parent us?"
"I think it's improvising. The whole System feels like jazz — brilliant, chaotic, making it up as it goes."
"What if the monsters are drafts? Sketches it didn't finish? We're living in someone's sketchbook."
monsters: "What if the monsters are scared of us too? We're the aliens here. Maybe they're the locals and we're the invasive species."
"What if we tried feeding one? Not fighting, not fleeing — just leaving food out. See what happens. Worst case, we're out a meal."
"They're beautiful, in a way. Terrifying, but beautiful. Like the world dreamed them up and the dream got loose."
"I name them. Not the System names — my names. It makes them less scary. Names are handles. You can grip a handle."
"What if they're not from here OR there? What if they're from the space between — the static when the world changed channels?"
"I draw them. Every one I see. Someday someone will need these drawings. Art outlives the artist, right?"
"They move like music. There's rhythm to it. Once you hear the rhythm, you can dance around them."
monstersGated: "The Hushpuppy doesn't want to kill you — it wants quiet. It's not a predator, it's a librarian with teeth."
situation: "We should throw a feast. I know — food's short. But a feast says 'we're going to make it,' and right now nobody believes that."
"What if we made the village beautiful? Paint the hall, hang things. Morale is a resource too — maybe the most important one."
"We keep trying to survive. What if we tried to thrive instead? Just as an experiment. See what changes."
"We need stories. Not just survival — narrative. People die without a story to live inside."
"What if we're the beginning of something? Like, mythic beginning. The old stories started exactly like this."
"I'm collecting moments. The good ones. Someday I'll tell them right, and they'll keep us warm."
"Despair is just imagination with no hope in it. So I imagine harder. With hope."
"We're writing the first chapter. Make it a good one. Future people are reading."

system: "Whatever it is, panicking doesn't help. Breathe. Watch. Learn. We've survived worse than confusion."
"It's not going away, so we adapt. That's what people do. We've always done it."
"Don't worship it, don't fight it. Just work around it. Like bad weather or a difficult neighbor."
"It's here. It's not leaving. Panicking about it wastes energy. Work with what is."
"I don't need to understand it fully. I need to understand it enough. Enough is achievable."
"Systems change. This one changed everything. We adapt. Adapting is what we do."
"It's consistent. That's what matters. Consistent things can be planned around."
"Worrying about its motives doesn't fill the pantry. Focus on what's in front of you."
monsters: "They're dangerous, yes. So's a river in flood. You respect it, you learn it, you don't let it rule you."
"One step at a time. Learn one monster's pattern. Then another. Nobody needs to know everything today."
"Fear makes them bigger than they are. Look at what's actually there, not what you're afraid is there."
"They're dangerous. That's the whole analysis. Respect the danger, take precautions, move on."
"Fear is data. It tells you where the threat is. Listen to it, then act anyway."
"We've handled worse. Not really, but saying it helps. Morale is logistics."
"Routine keeps you alive. Check the perimeter. Same time. Every time. Boring saves lives."
"Don't get creative with monsters. Creative gets you killed. Boring and careful gets you home."
situation: "We'll get through today. Then tomorrow. That's how this works — one day at a time, same as always."
"Everyone's scared. That's fine. Scared people can still carry water and chop wood. Feel it and do the work anyway."
"Let's not borrow trouble. Right now: we're fed, we're sheltered, we're together. That's enough for today."
"One day at a time. That's not a platitude — it's a strategy. The future's too big to carry."
"We're doing fine. Look at us. Breathing, talking, planning. That's winning."
"Bad days end. They always end. I've seen enough of them to know."
"Keep the rhythm. Meals, watches, sleep. Rhythm is what separates a camp from a crowd."
"It's okay to not be okay. It's not okay to stop. We keep going. That's the deal."

analytical: "I've been thinking about the pattern in all this..."
"Have you noticed? It never does the same thing twice — except when it does."
"Question for you: what do you think it actually wants from us?"
"I've been charting when things happen. There's a rhythm. I haven't found the downbeat yet."
"Three data points make a pattern. I've got two. Help me find the third."
"Everyone's theorizing. I'm testing. There's a difference, and it matters."
practical: "Walk with me — I could use an extra pair of hands."
"Got a minute? Something needs doing and I'd rather not do it alone."
"While I've got you — help me think through tomorrow's work."
"That lean-to won't fix itself. Grab an end?"
"I need a second opinion — and a second pair of hands. You've got both."
"While you're here: does this look straight to you? Be honest."
social: "Have you talked to the others lately? I'm a little worried about the mood."
"Something's shifting in the group. You feel it too, right?"
"Can I ask you something — person to person, not village business?"
"Okay, be honest with me — how are people REALLY doing? I get the performance version."
"I think two people are fighting and neither will say it. Am I imagining things?"
"Who haven't you talked to in a while? Go talk to them. I'll wait."
observant: "Did you see that, just now? By the tree line."
"Something's different today. Can't quite place it yet."
"Look at the fire — see how it's leaning? Wind's changing."
"The birds went quiet an hour ago. They haven't started again. Noting it."
"You've got a tell when you're worried. Just so you know. It's the jaw thing."
"Count the fireflies with me? No reason. Just — count them."
creative: "Okay, hear me out — what if we're thinking about this all wrong?"
"I had the strangest idea last night. Tell me if I'm crazy."
"What if — just what if — the monsters aren't the problem?"
"What if we're the entertainment AND the experiment? Both. Simultaneously."
"I keep having this image — us, years from now, laughing about this. I want it to be true."
"New theory. It's stupid. That's how you know it might be right."
steady: "How are you holding up? Honestly. No performance."
"Got a moment? No rush. Just wanted to check in."
"Sit with me a minute. The work'll keep."
"Checking in. No agenda. How's your head?"
"I've got tea. Well — hot leaf water. But it's warm and I'm sharing."
"Walk the perimeter with me? Quiet company. No big talk."

familiarity._comment: Familiarity: what you know of the land you landed in, from where you are from (origin vs landing). Tiers are checked best-first: native = your lifeseed sub-area lists this landing variant as home ground; local = same world region; neighbor = the regions border (regions.json neighbors, either side); visitor = same climateFamily; stranger = anything else. plants = how many plants each roster member knows at the start; plantLevel = the codex level of the player's own starting plants; animals = which common animals you can name: pool (every common animal of this land), continent (common animals of your continent or your own tags), overlap (only animals tagged with your own origin tags); animalLevel = codex depth seeded for the pool animals (0 = none); say = the opening line (empty = none).

native.say: This is home ground. You grew up on country like this.

neighbor.say: This is the country next door to home. Some of it you know.

visitor.say: Some of this country feels familiar. Not enough.
